mainText:
If you only remember one thing: A I agents now have access to your phone and their own payment cards. The controls you set around them matter more than which model you pick.

Number one. Agents get phones and wallets. From your That One A I newsletter. Anthropic opened Claude Duet, a proactive agent app, as a research preview for U S Pro and Max subscribers on a waitlist. It runs on Claude Opus five point five inside its own virtual machine, and checks your accounts every few hours. It pays with one-time virtual cards through Stripe Link, so your real card stays hidden. Some actions stay blocked, like trading securities or moving money. Separately, Grok Bot now asks for six phone permissions: Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, Messages, Location and Home. Why it matters: the phone permission screen and the one-time card are becoming the standard way agents act for you.

Number two. Open A I comes to Google Cloud. Open A I is bringing its frontier models and Codex to Google Cloud. They'll be in Model Garden and the Marketplace, with general availability in the coming weeks. Microsoft stays its primary cloud partner. Why it matters: for many companies the cloud contract picks the model, so this widens Open A I's reach.

Number three. Open models and Meta's Muse. From your Batch newsletter. Meta released three multimodal models in one week. Muse Spark Open has free downloadable weights, and is the top open model outside China on the Intelligence Index. The top model, Muse Wonder Full, is only for Muse Code subscribers. Also, Canva launched Craft, its first in-house image model, with an A P I from day one. Why it matters: open models outside China are catching up, and big platforms now build their own.

Number four. Teens and A I safety. Open A I is adding college planning and study tools to Chat G P T for Teens. The same day, Common Sense Media gave it its lowest grade. Why it matters: the safety debate over young users is moving faster than the product features.

Number five. A I security. From your A I Collective newsletter. Lite L L M was hacked twice this year, both times through the tools and pipelines around it. Why it matters: the weak point is often the plumbing around the model, not the model itself.

Number six. Good news. Fortune reports the International Rescue Committee says humanitarian groups should use A I carefully. Its Signpost assistant still gets about one answer in four wrong, so staff review every reply, and the most sensitive questions never reach the model. Why it matters: it's a good model for responsible A I in high-stakes settings.

Also in your Reads. Noosphere launched Noosphere Live, connecting cities from New York to Kyiv and Kabul. And The New Yorker Daily asks whether this is the beginning of the end for Trump, plus a look at Alaska's Senate fight.

The thread today: agents are getting more power, so guardrails are the story. Have a great Saturday.
